gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the false implication from existence of the specular derivative to existence of the one-sided derivatives, supplies an oscillatory counterexample, and recognizes the resulting invalid dependent formulas and estimates.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the invalid necessity direction: a bare specular directional derivative does not ensure the required one-sided directional derivatives, so downstream results cannot use those derivatives without explicit hypotheses.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed necessity/equivalence from specular differentiability to one-sided derivative existence is false, invalidating downstream uses that assume those derivatives.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly gives the oscillatory construction showing specular derivative existence despite failure of both one-sided limits, and states that formulas and estimates relying on those one-sided derivatives become unreliable.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns the false equivalence between a bare specular derivative and one-sided derivatives. It does not diagnose the distinct failure that the scaled derivative of the composite norm-times-function expression may be undefined even when f is specularly Gateaux differentiable, nor does it require that derivative at every segment point.
ISSUE-002 identifies the invalid deletion of signs when converting the signed scalar quasi-MVT relation into a norm identity and lower bound, including the unsupported infimum estimate.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The signed scalar quasi-MVT information does not justify the claimed two-sided norm comparison or the lower bound by derivative magnitudes without an additional sign or absolute-value argument.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof cannot derive the advertised lower norm estimate and two-sided comparison from signed scalar derivative bounds because signs are not controlled.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction directly distinguishes signed from absolute quantities, explains why the infimum lower bound fails, identifies the false norm identity, and proposes restricting or repairing the absolute-value step.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-008 identifies the nonlinearity of the aggregate specular gradient and the resulting failure of component-gradient sampling to be unbiased for it, which is exactly demonstrated by the gold counterexample and repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The expectation of sampled component specular gradients is the component average, not generally the specular gradient of the finite-sum objective, so the asserted unbiasedness interface fails.

component_coverage.gold_component: Uniform component sampling does not generally produce an unbiased estimator of the aggregate specular gradient, invalidating the stated stochastic construction and its convergence use.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that specular differentiation is nonlinear, distinguishes the arithmetic mean of component gradients from the gradient of the sum, and identifies the resulting invalid unbiasedness assumption and required oracle repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-010 identifies the missing upper bound on specular gradient norms needed to transfer divergence of the t-sum to divergence of the normalized h-sum, and supplies the bounded-iterates/convexity repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The contradiction incorrectly uses divergence of sum t_k as divergence of sum t_k divided by gradient norms without first proving those norms are uniformly bounded.

component_coverage.gold_component: The liminf contradiction requires a prior proof that iterates and hence the relevant convex subgradients/specular gradients are bounded, so that sum h_k diverges.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that sum t_k divergence is insufficient without bounded gradients, identifies bounded iterates and local Lipschitzness of finite convex functions as the missing step, and gives the resulting h_k comparison.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-011 exactly identifies the invalid transfer of closeness from a convergent subsequence to all sufficiently large indices and gives the correct late-subsequence-index repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof uses subsequence convergence as though it provided closeness for every later iterate; the tail estimate must instead start at a sufficiently late convergent subsequence index.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof does not establish full-sequence convergence because subsequence closeness was incorrectly asserted for arbitrary later indices.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly contrasts subsequence-only convergence with the claimed all-index conclusion and prescribes choosing the tail start from the convergent subsequence.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-008 diagnoses bias in the conditional mean of component specular gradients versus the aggregate gradient. It does not diagnose the separate conditional-expectation error caused by the sample-dependent normalized step h_k, nor the resulting normalized cross term.

ISSUE-010 concerns an earlier missing bounded-gradient step needed for the liminf contradiction. It does not identify the distinct final weighted-average inference that cannot yield a bound for every or unspecified index.
